blocking_findings.title: The row wrapper can be made to launch in a non-canonical execution directory
evidence: launch_generation.py:136-144 counts only argv elements exactly equal to --execution-directory and validates only the following element.
The sealed S35 parser at launch_original.py:453-455 also accepts --execution-directory=<value> and resolves repeated options by taking the last value.

On both Python 3.13.0 and Python 3.12.14, the wrapper accepted --execution-directory <canonical execution_01> --execution-directory=/tmp/s47-c2-adversarial-bypass, while downstream argparse selected /tmp/s47-c2-adversarial-bypass.
launch_generation.py also accepts a caller-supplied --worker token; the sealed parent dispatches directly to worker(args) at launch_original.py:460.
blocking_findings.impact: An authorized caller can route the launch receipt to an arbitrary fresh directory while leaving the reviewed execution_01 path unused. In particular, failures before output-root creation can be retried through further alternate directories, so the fixed-path and one-attempt claims in PROTOCOL.md:34 are not enforced. The accepted worker flag also exposes the parent's internal worker route to the external CLI instead of reserving it to the monitored parent process.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Parse and normalize the complete outer CLI once; reject duplicate or equals-form execution-directory options, argparse abbreviations, and every external worker-mode request. Pass a sanitized canonical argument object to the derived parent. If an internal worker mode remains necessary, authenticate it with a parent-created create-only capability that cannot be supplied through the public wrapper. Re-run the two-interpreter adversarial argv tests.

blocking_findings.title: Bound identities are hashed and then reopened for parsing or execution
evidence: generation_gate.py:249-252, 256-257, 350-351, 478-479, 495-498, and 545-549 hash a pathname and then reopen it for JSON parsing.
freeze_c2_manifest.py:105-111 and create_launch_authorization.py:95-102 hash generation_gate.py and then execute a later pathname lookup through SourceFileLoader.
freeze_c2_manifest.py:74-77 and create_launch_authorization.py:45-54 perform the same hash-then-read sequence for bound JSON records.
runtime_adapter.py:24-25 hashes the S35 factory and then reopens it for AST parsing.
blocking_findings.impact: A pathname replacement between the hash and the second open lets the bytes parsed or executed differ from the bytes whose SHA was approved. The dynamic-import cases may also select cached bytecode. Rechecking a pathname later does not prove that the intervening parse or execution used the approved bytes, so source, review, manifest, and authorization bindings are not fail-closed against the requested TOCTOU adversary.
blocking_findings.required_fix: For each bound source or JSON record, open once with O_NOFOLLOW, verify a regular file and expected device/inode/mode from fstat, read one immutable byte snapshot, hash that snapshot, and parse or compile those exact bytes. Avoid SourceFileLoader for bound code; compile the verified bytes directly. Hold directory/file leases or revalidate the same descriptor identity across publication-sensitive phases.

blocking_findings.title: A failed authorization staging attempt does not consume a fixed attempt lease
evidence: PROTOCOL.md:33 says create_launch_authorization.py may run once.
create_launch_authorization.py:177-184 chooses a new PID/time-nanosecond staging pathname on every invocation.

create_launch_authorization.py:185-189 has no terminal failure handler or fixed create-only attempt marker; require_formal_freshness at lines 106-109 checks only the final authorization, execution_01, and output root.
blocking_findings.impact: If an invocation fails after writing its staging file but before publishing launch_authorization_01.json, the next invocation selects a different staging name and is accepted while the fixed authorization remains absent. Thus authorization staging can be retried despite the stated one-run contract, and abandoned staging artifacts are neither authoritative terminal failures nor gates on later attempts.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Claim a fixed create-only authorization-attempt lease before staging and retain a terminal success or failure record under that lease. Make every later invocation fail when the lease exists. If prepublication retries are intended, revise the protocol explicitly and bind a retry counter and all retained failures into the terminal authorization review.

blocking_findings.title: The unpublished-metadata exception is not restricted to the attach preflight object
evidence: generation_gate.py:667-678 checks only that _allow_unpublished_attachment implies metadata_only, then skips both require_published_attachment and require_launch_authorization.
No check binds the exception to freeze_c2_manifest.py's temporary candidate, rejects PUBLISHED_MANIFEST, or proves that the authorization and canonical attachment are absent.
The returned status at generation_gate.py:718-733 remains PASS_METADATA_ONLY, although execution_authorized is false.
blocking_findings.impact: Any caller can request the private flag for the canonical published manifest and receive a metadata PASS before authorization. This does not by itself produce a full resource gate, but it contradicts PROTOCOL.md:34 and FREEZE_PROTOCOL.md:16, which state that the exception is solely for the temporary non-authoritative attach preflight and that canonical published metadata gates require authorization.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Remove the caller-controlled boolean from the general gate API. Validate a byte snapshot through a narrowly scoped attach-preflight function or an unforgeable in-process capability, and explicitly reject PUBLISHED_MANIFEST and every path outside the active hidden staging directory when authorization is absent.

blocking_findings.title: Runtime evidence path selection and temporary publication are replaceable
evidence: runtime_adapter.py:81 validates the supplied gate, but lines 83-85 reopen gate[manifest_path] without a bound snapshot and use that second document to choose output_root/runtime_loading.json.

runtime_adapter.py:151-156 writes the predictable runtime_loading.s47-c2.tmp with ordinary write_text before replace; it neither uses create-exclusive O_NOFOLLOW creation nor holds the output directory identity.
blocking_findings.impact: A concurrent manifest replacement can redirect the runtime-loading record after gate validation. A pre-existing temporary symlink can make write_text follow and truncate another writable target. These paths violate the requested path-replacement and create-only evidence guarantees.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Carry the already verified manifest/output identity in the gate object and do not reopen the manifest for routing. Hold an output-directory descriptor, create a randomized or fixed leased temporary file relative to that descriptor with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, fsync it, verify descriptor identity, and publish relative to the same directory descriptor without following symlinks.
